questions.q: Why does the summary say rookies have an advantage at work?
a: Knowledge changes fast and rookies are not set in their ways
Rookies have more experience than older workers
Rookies demand lower salaries than anyone else
Rookies already know the company's best practices
questions.why: The overview says rapid change rewards learners who are not bound by the status quo.

questions.q: What did Buckminster Fuller show about human knowledge?
a: The time it takes to double keeps shrinking rapidly
Knowledge now doubles every hundred years
Knowledge has stopped growing since the internet
Most knowledge is lost within a century
questions.why: Lesson 1 traces doubling times from 1,500 years down to about 12 months today.

questions.q: What is opinion stasis in the summary?
a: Being so settled in your views that change becomes hard
The habit of asking too many questions at work
A fear of speaking in front of a team
Refusing to learn from younger colleagues
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes experienced people who struggle to change their ways and surround themselves with people who agree.

questions.q: How do rookies sometimes outsmart experienced coworkers?
a: By asking questions and seeking help from experts
By hiding their lack of knowledge from others
By working longer hours than everyone else
By copying whatever the team already does
questions.why: Lesson 2 says rookies reach out to experts far more often, and that asking for help builds real expertise.

questions.q: How can an experienced person regain rookie smarts?
a: By putting themselves into learning mode again
By avoiding unfamiliar tasks at work
By mentoring younger employees only
By waiting for the company to retrain them
questions.why: Lesson 3 says rookie smarts are a mindset anyone can cultivate by volunteering, swapping jobs or reading something new.
